subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw define and support a runtime-neutral agent-core protocol for no-Node embedded or WASM ports, or should those ports remain independent external projects without a core compatibility contract?
rationale: Current source and docs still make OpenClaw Node-hosted, while accepting this request would affect core runtime ownership, plugin SDK boundaries, storage/session semantics, providers, tools, and security policy.

options.title: Keep As Runtime-Portability RFC
options.body: Use this issue to design the minimal schemas, conformance tests, and ownership boundary before accepting an embedded or WASM implementation.

options.title: Scope To Plugin SDK Only
options.body: Route near-term language/runtime work through JSON-RPC/plugin-harness APIs and leave full no-Node ports outside the supported OpenClaw contract.

options.title: Close As Not Planned
options.body: Decide that OpenClaw remains Node-hosted and external projects such as MimiClaw are independent ports without compatibility promises.

recommendation.title: Keep As Runtime-Portability RFC
recommendation.body: Use this issue to design the minimal schemas, conformance tests, and ownership boundary before accepting an embedded or WASM implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest current issue-discussion and harness/runtime-direction history signal for deciding the product boundary.
